solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Certain cheats — zany characters with musical instruments

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person, so zany characters are cards
harps are stringed musical instruments

explanation.surface: Some swindlers turn out to be eccentric types who play the harp.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'card' is informal for a joker or eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who cheats at card games, so these are one particular kind of cheat.

clue.text: Jargon philosopher's spoken

indicators.note: spoken tells us the philosopher's name is heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Immanuel Kant is the German philosopher; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A philosopher's talk is dismissed as mere jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: KANT, the philosopher, said aloud gives a word spelt with a C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is the specialised vocabulary or slang of a particular group, a synonym for jargon.

clue.text: Lines of angry exchanges?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lines of things side by side
second meaning: ... (rhyming with cows) are noisy quarrels

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but pronounced differently, which the question mark acknowledges.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both straight lines of seats or plants and heated quarrels, pronounced differently in each sense.

clue.text: Senior cop rushed, full of emotion

parts.note: super is short for superintendent, a senior police officer
to charge is to rush forward at something

explanation.surface: A police superintendent charges in, worked up and emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPER is British slang for a police superintendent.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercharged atmosphere is intensely charged with feeling, so highly emotional.

clue.text: Jelly with a flavour that's inadequate

indicators.note: inadequate says the word falls short, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: spice gives food its flavour

explanation.surface: A jelly whose taste is disappointingly weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is just a link joining the A to the shortened flavour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Appropriate as some expert in entertainment

indicators.note: as some of the following words, so the answer is found within them

explanation.surface: Suitable behaviour for a professional in show business.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through exPERT IN ENTertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent means relevant to the matter at hand, so apt or fitting.

clue.text: Pole left over, a bit short

indicators.note: a bit short says the word is cut by one letter at its end

parts.note: spare means left over, surplus

explanation.surface: A pole that is surplus but slightly too short for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit short' trims the last letter of SPARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole, such as a mast or boom on a ship.

clue.text: Forecast offered by professional theologian regarded as heretic

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a Gnostic belonged to an early religious movement condemned by the Church as heretical

explanation.surface: A prediction made by a professional churchman thought to be heretical.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognostic is a sign or prediction of what will happen, as in a medical prognosis.

clue.text: My daughter is entertained by funny singer in studio productions

indicators.note: is entertained by means is taken inside, as a guest is welcomed into a home
funny signals that the letters of singer are put in an odd order

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: A girl is amused by an eccentric vocalist at a recording studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive here but the exclamation, as in British 'cor!' for surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Recordings are what a studio produces: audio or video tracks captured for playback.

clue.text: Publications not mainly in the pink!

definitions.text: Publications not mainly in the pink!

parts.words: Publications not mainly in the pink
parts.note: the Financial Times is famously printed on pink paper, but most of its rivals are printed on white

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' sounds like good health, but it refers to the pink pages of the Financial Times, where this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily papers are publications, and nearly all of them use white rather than the pink stock of the Financial Times.

clue.text: Necklace is light, not hard

indicators.note: not says the following letter is to be left out

parts.note: a torch is a hand-held light
h is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A necklace is described as lightweight and soft.
explanation.walkthrough: A torch is the British word for a flashlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a rigid neck ring of twisted metal worn by ancient Celts.

clue.text: Slam Blairite involved in two-sided negotiations

indicators.note: involved means twisted up together, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A political attack on a Tony Blair supporter during talks between two parties.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blairite is a follower of former British Prime Minister Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateralism is the conduct of relations or deals between two parties, so talks with two sides.

clue.text: Professional criterion apt to be flexible

indicators.note: flexible letters can bend into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A professional's standards should be adaptable when appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner is someone who practises a profession, such as a doctor or lawyer.

clue.text: New signora excited certain natives

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A newly arrived Italian lady gets the locals worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwegians are people born in Norway, one particular nation's natives.

clue.text: Upset tot a yeller? I'll bring a drink round

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A distressed toddler bawls while someone promises to fetch something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A tea trolley is a wheeled cart once pushed round British offices and hospitals serving tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea trolley is a cart that brings cups of tea round to people, speaking here in the first person.

clue.text: Hospitality old writer Henry established by river

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
h is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A welcome offered by an elderly author named Henry living beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex).
explanation.definitionFit: Open house means welcoming all visitors freely, a generous form of hospitality.

clue.text: Maybe propping up team that is bottom?

parts.note: something propping up another thing sits under it
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A football club languishing at the foot of the league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Propping up' the table is a British idiom for being last in a league.
explanation.definitionFit: The underside is the lower surface of something, its bottom.

clue.text: Very foolish person by Great North Road

parts.note: an ass is a fool
the A1 is the British trunk road following the old Great North Road; its digit 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An idiot standing beside a famous highway.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 reads as AI: the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian musical direction meaning very, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Rebel with hesitation in river?

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A rebel hesitates before fording a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: the answer is what is found in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a flowing body of water, so this is what fills one.

clue.text: Hesitant princess starting operatic cycle

indicators.note: starting places the princess at the beginning of the cycle

parts.note: Di is Princess Diana
The Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas

explanation.surface: A nervous princess begins a long Wagner opera series.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithering means being indecisive, unable to make up one's mind.

clue.text: I repeatedly get romance wrong — I cannot square the circle!

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: I taken twice, then the letters of get romance as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps getting love wrong, then laments an impossible task.
explanation.walkthrough: Squaring the circle, constructing a square equal in area to a given circle, is a famous impossible problem of geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometrician is a mathematician of shapes; squaring the circle with compass and ruler is proved impossible.

clue.text: Officer in charge is a pain

parts.note: col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: The commanding officer is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Officer in charge' reads as one title, but it is two abbreviations: a colonel, then the label for in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is a severe abdominal pain, typically in babies or horses.

clue.text: Hospital hooter making a beastly noise?

parts.note: h is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an owl hoots

explanation.surface: A hospital's alarm siren makes a horrible racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a horn or alarm, but here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A howl is the long wailing cry of an animal such as a wolf or dog.

clue.text: Like one area, an area very large

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Comparing one region with another enormous one.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, a vast region of the globe.

clue.text: Skilful learner taken on board by former President

indicators.note: taken on board by means held within, so the learner goes inside the President's name

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the 16th US President
l is the learner plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A talented trainee is hired by an ex-president.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plate a British learner driver displays.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable or competent at doing something, a synonym for skilled.

clue.text: Very bad adult, one with common sense, very bad

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects
a is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
the Roman numeral I is one
nous is British informal for practical good sense

explanation.surface: A wicked grown-up who is nonetheless shrewd is described as awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue starts and ends with 'very bad': the first pair is wordplay, the last the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Villainous means wicked or criminal, like a villain, or figuratively dreadful.

clue.text: Yen to be in specialist fighting unit in States

indicators.note: to be in means placed inside, so the yen goes into the unit

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service
y is the abbreviation for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A longing to join an elite military unit in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like America, but it is the verb meaning declares.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to say it; both verbs mean declare.

clue.text: Sweet chap, me, 24, roughly

indicators.note: roughly means approximately, not in exact order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the answer to 24 across, a word for skilful

explanation.surface: A man describes himself as a lovely fellow, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The 24 stands for ABLE, the answer at 24 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Peach Melba is a dessert of peaches, raspberry sauce and ice cream, named after the soprano Nellie Melba.
